# developer.paypal.com documentation — Braintree — Docs — Start

> 27 page(s) of developer.paypal.com documentation — Braintree — Docs under Start. Part of the index one level up (../llms.txt).

## Start

- [Overview](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/overview/): This guide will walk you through a basic Braintree Direct integration that accepts credit card payments in sandbox using our Drop-in UI.
- [Drop-in UI](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/drop-in): We provide complementary client- and server-side SDKs to complete your integration: The **client SDKs** enable you to collect payment method (e.g. credit card, PayPal) details.
- [Hosted Fields](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/hosted-fields): Hosted Fields is a way to accept credit card payments securely using our JavaScript SDK, while staying in control of the style of your desktop and mobile website checkout UI.
- [Drop-in Tutorial](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/tutorial-drop-in-node): First, make sure you have the latest versions of [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/) and [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/get-npm) installed. You’ll also need a console (e.g.
- [Using the Examples](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/example-integrations-drop-in/using-the-examples): The end-to-end example integrations are made to run on a local server or on Heroku.
- [Set Up Your Client](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/hello-client/): To start up, Braintree.js needs a client token generated by your Braintree server SDK.
- [Set Up Your Server](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/hello-server/): The SSL certificates for all Braintree SDKs are set to expire by March 30, 2026. This will impact existing versions of the SDK in published versions of your app.
